meta.prompt: You are a worldclass math professor with expertise in breaking down math problems into easy to understand, coherent step

steps.title: Understand the Setup
steps.description:
We have Circle $O$ with radius $12$ cm. Points $A$ and $B$ sit on the circle, and the **central angle** $\angle AOB = 60°$. Since $OA$ and $OB$ are both radii, triangle $AOB$ is **isosceles** with $OA = OB = 12$ cm.

For **(a)**, we need the straight-line distance $AB$ (the chord).
For **(b)**, we need the curved distance along the circle from $A$ to $B$ (the arc).

The key insight for part (a): when an isosceles triangle also has its apex angle equal to $60°$, all three angles must be $60°$ — making it **equilateral**. That collapses a trig formula into a one-liner.

steps.title: Identify the Equilateral Triangle
steps.description:
Triangle $AOB$ is isosceles with $OA = OB = 12$ cm and apex angle $\angle AOB = 60°$.

The two base angles must share the remaining $180° - 60° = 120°$ equally:
$$\angle OAB = \angle OBA = \frac{120°}{2} = 60°$$

All three angles are $60°$, so triangle $AOB$ is **equilateral**. In an equilateral triangle every side equals every other side, so:
$$AB = OA = OB = 12 \text{ cm}$$

steps.title: Find the Arc Length
steps.description:
The arc length formula scales the full circumference by the fraction of the circle that the central angle represents:
$$\ell = \frac{\theta}{360°} \times 2\pi r$$

Substituting $\theta = 60°$ and $r = 12$:
$$\ell = \frac{60°}{360°} \times 2\pi (12) = \frac{1}{6} \times 24\pi = 4\pi \text{ cm}$$
